title.zh: 卷二百八十六 列傳第四十五 魯宗道 薛奎 王曙 蔡齊
title.en: Volume 286 Biographies 45: Lu Zongdao, Xue Kui, Wang Shu, Cai Qi
title.raw: 卷二百八十六 列傳第四十五 魯宗道 薛奎 王曙 蔡齊 Volume 286 Biographies 45: Lu Zongdao, Xue Kui, Wang Shu, Cai Qi

sentences.zh: 魯宗道

translations.literal: Lu Zongdao
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongdao

sentences.zh: 魯宗道，字貫之，亳州譙人。

translations.literal: Lu Zongdao, styled Guanzhi, was a native of Qiao in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongdao, whose courtesy name was Guanzhi, came from Qiao in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，鞠於外家。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he was reared in his maternal kin's household.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents while still young and was brought up in the home of his mother's family.

sentences.zh: 諸舅皆武人，頗易宗道，宗道益自奮厲讀書。

translations.literal: His maternal uncles were all military men and looked down on Zongdao somewhat; Zongdao thereupon strove all the harder in his studies.
translations.idiomatic: His uncles on his mother's side were soldiers who tended to treat him lightly, which only made him drive himself harder in his reading.

sentences.zh: 袖所著文謁戚綸，綸器重之。

translations.literal: With his own writings tucked in his sleeve he called on Qi Lun, and Lun regarded him with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: He went to see Qi Lun carrying essays he had written in his sleeve, and Lun was deeply impressed by him.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為濠州定遠尉，再調海鹽令。

translations.literal: Having passed the jinshi examination, he became defender of Dingyuan in Haozhou and was later transferred to magistrate of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: After earning his jinshi degree, he served as assistant magistrate of Dingyuan in Haozhou and was later reassigned as magistrate of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 縣東南舊有港，導海水至邑下，歲久堙塞，宗道發鄉丁疏治之，人號“魯公浦”。

translations.literal: Southeast of the county there had long been a channel that conducted seawater to below the seat; after many years it had silted shut. Zongdao mobilized local militiamen to dredge and repair it, and people called it "Duke Lu's Creek."
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the county lay an old channel that had once brought seawater to the town, but it had long since silted up. Zongdao called out the local militia to clear and repair it, and the people nicknamed it "Duke Lu's Channel."

sentences.zh: 改歙州軍事判官，再遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military administrative assistant of Shezhou and was later promoted to secretary in the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the post of military administrative assistant in Shezhou, then promoted to secretary in the palace archive.

sentences.zh: 陳堯叟辟通判河陽。

translations.literal: Chen Yaosou recruited him as supervisory commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yaosou brought him in as supervisory commissioner of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，始詔兩省置諫官六員，考所言為殿最，首擢宗道與劉燁為右正言。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi, an edict first established six remonstrating officials in the two departments of the Secretariat, ranking their memorials as evaluations; Zongdao and Liu Ye were first promoted as Right Rectifiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianxi reign, the court for the first time ordered six remonstrance officers set up in the eastern and western secretariats and graded their remonstrances for merit review. Zongdao and Liu Ye were the first appointed as Right Rectifiers.

sentences.zh: 諫章由閣門始得進而不賜對，宗道請面論事而上奏通進司，遂為故事。

translations.literal: Remonstrance memorials had first to pass through the palace gate office and could be submitted but were not granted audience. Zongdao requested to discuss matters face to face and submit memorials through the general memorial office, and this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Until then remonstrance memorials had to go through the Gate Office before submission and were not granted a personal audience. Zongdao asked to discuss affairs in person and to submit memorials through the general memorial office instead, and that became established practice.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：“守宰去民近，而無以區別能否。

translations.literal: He once said: "Prefects and magistrates are closest to the people, yet there is no means to distinguish the capable from the incapable.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Prefects and magistrates stand closest to the people, yet we have no reliable way to tell who is capable and who is not.

sentences.zh: 今除一守令，雖資材低下，而考任應格，則左司無擯斥，故天下親民者黷貨害政，十常二三，欲裕民而美化，不可得矣。

translations.literal: Today when a prefect or magistrate is appointed, even if his talent is low yet his examination and tenure meet the standard, the left office has no grounds to reject him. Therefore among those who are close to the people across the realm, those who enrich themselves by corruption and harm governance are often two or three in ten. To enrich the people and beautify government is unattainable.
translations.idiomatic: Today when a prefect or magistrate is appointed, even a man of mediocre talent cannot be rejected so long as his service review meets the formal requirements. Across the empire, officials who deal directly with the people corrupt their offices and ruin governance—perhaps two or three in ten—and under such conditions there is no hope of enriching the people and improving government.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝除刺史守相，必親見而考察之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan of Han appointed regional inspectors, prefects, and chancellors, he always received them in person and examined them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan of Han appointed regional inspectors, prefects, and counselors, he always met them in person and tested their fitness for office.

sentences.zh: 今守佐雖未暇親見，宜令大臣延之中書，詢考以言，察其應對，設之以事，觀其施為才不肖，皆得進退之。

translations.literal: Now though prefects and assistants cannot all be seen in person for lack of time, the senior ministers should be ordered to summon them to the Central Secretariat, inquire and examine them by speech, observe their responses, set them tasks, and watch their conduct to see whether they are talented or not, so that all may be promoted or dismissed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the emperor cannot meet every prefect and assistant in person, he should have senior ministers summon them to the Secretariat, question them, observe how they answer, set them tasks, and watch how they perform, so that promotion and dismissal may rest on genuine merit.

sentences.zh: 吏部之擇縣令放此，庶得良守宰宣助聖化矣。”

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel's selection of county magistrates should follow this pattern; then perhaps good prefects and magistrates may be obtained to proclaim and assist the sage's transformation."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel should apply the same procedure in choosing county magistrates, so that worthy local officials may be found to carry forward the emperor's civilizing rule."

sentences.zh: 真宗納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong adopted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 宗道風聞，多所論列，帝意頗厭其數。

translations.literal: Zongdao had information from hearsay and discussed many matters; the emperor's mind grew rather weary of how often he did so.
translations.idiomatic: Zongdao heard reports of abuses and remonstrated frequently; the emperor grew annoyed at his persistence.

sentences.zh: 後因對，自訟曰：“陛下用臣，豈欲徒事納諫之虛名邪？

translations.literal: Later, in an audience, he accused himself, saying: "Your Majesty employs me—surely you do not wish only the empty reputation of accepting remonstrance?
translations.idiomatic: Later, in an audience, he rebuked himself, saying: "Your Majesty has put me in office. Surely you did not mean to gain only the empty reputation of accepting remonstrance?

sentences.zh: 臣竊恥屍祿，請得罷去。”

translations.literal: I secretly shame myself for holding salary without merit; I beg to be dismissed and leave."
translations.idiomatic: I am ashamed to draw salary without earning it. Please let me resign."

sentences.zh: 帝撫諭良久，他日書殿壁曰：“魯直”，蓋思念之也。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted and instructed him for a long while. Another day he wrote on the palace wall: "Straight Lu," presumably in remembrance of him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him at length. On another day he wrote on a palace wall the words "Straight Lu," evidently missing him.

sentences.zh: 尋除戶部員外郎兼右諭德。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently Right Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently Right Tutor.

sentences.zh: 逾年，遷左諭德、直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was transferred to Left Tutor and appointed to the Longtu Pavilion as a direct appointee.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was promoted to Left Tutor and made a direct appointee of the Longtu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷戶部郎中、龍圖閣直學士兼侍講、判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, Zongdao was transferred to director in the Ministry of Revenue, Associate Academician of the Longtu Pavilion, concurrent court reader, and director of the Ministry of Personnel's mobile selection office.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, he was made director of the Ministry of Revenue, associate academician of the Longtu Pavilion, court reader, and supervisor of the mobile selection office in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宗道在選調久，患銓格煩密，及知吏所以為奸狀，多厘正之，悉揭科條廡下，人便之。

translations.literal: Zongdao had long been in appointments and transfers, and grieved that the examination rules were tedious and detailed. Once he knew how clerks committed malfeasance, he corrected much of it, posted all regulations and statutes in the hall below, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Having long worked in personnel appointments, he hated how tangled and rigid the selection rules had become. Once he understood how clerks were cheating, he corrected many abuses and posted all regulations in the hall so that everyone could see them, which made the office far easier to use.

sentences.zh: 雷允恭擅易山陵，詔與呂夷簡等按視。

translations.literal: Lei Yungong had altered the imperial tomb without authorization; an edict ordered Zongdao together with Lü Yijian and others to investigate and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: When Lei Yungong altered the imperial tomb without authority, the court ordered Zongdao to investigate alongside Lü Yijian and others.

sentences.zh: 還，拜右諫議大夫、參知政事。

translations.literal: On his return, he was appointed Right Remonstrance Counselor and Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Right Remonstrance Counselor and vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后臨朝，問宗道曰：“唐武后何如主？”

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian held court, she asked Zongdao: "What sort of ruler was Empress Wu of Tang?"
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Dowager Zhangxian was regent, she asked Zongdao: "What kind of ruler was Empress Wu of Tang?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：“唐之罪人也，幾危社稷。”

translations.literal: He replied: "A criminal of Tang who nearly endangered the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "A criminal of the Tang who nearly brought down the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 后默然。

translations.literal: The empress was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress fell silent.

sentences.zh: 時有請立劉氏七廟者，太后問輔臣，眾不敢對。

translations.literal: At the time some requested establishing the seven ancestral temples of the Liu clan; the empress asked the chief ministers, and none dared answer.
translations.idiomatic: Some then proposed establishing the seven ancestral temples of the Liu clan. The empress asked the chief ministers, but none dared reply.

sentences.zh: 宗道不可，曰：“若立劉氏七廟，如嗣君何？”

translations.literal: Zongdao would not agree, saying: "If the Liu seven temples are established, what of the heir to the throne?"
translations.idiomatic: Zongdao objected, saying: "If the Liu temples are set up, what becomes of the heir apparent?"

sentences.zh: 帝、太后將同幸慈孝寺，欲以大安輦先帝行，宗道曰：“夫死從子，婦人之道也。”

translations.literal: The emperor and the empress were about to visit Cixiao Temple together and wished to have the great imperial palanquin go ahead with the late emperor's spirit tablet. Zongdao said: "When the husband dies, the wife follows the son—such is the way of women."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor and empress were about to visit Cixiao Temple together, they wanted the great imperial palanquin to go ahead carrying the late emperor's spirit tablet. Zongdao said: "When a husband dies, a wife follows her son—that is the proper order for a woman."

sentences.zh: 太后遽命輦后乘輿。

translations.literal: The empress immediately ordered the palanquin to follow behind the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The empress at once ordered the palanquin to follow behind her own carriage.

sentences.zh: 時執政多任子於館閣讀書，宗道曰：“館閣育天下英才，豈紈袴子弟得以恩澤處邪？”

translations.literal: At the time those in power often placed their sons in the Hanlin Academy to study. Zongdao said: "The Academy nurtures the empire's finest talents—how can the sons of silk-clad families occupy it through favor?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time those in power often placed their sons in the Hanlin Academy to study. Zongdao said: "The Academy exists to nurture the empire's finest talents. How can the sons of the privileged occupy it through favoritism?"

sentences.zh: 樞密使曹利用恃權驕橫，宗道屢於帝前折之。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of Military Affairs Cao Liyong relied on power and was arrogant; Zongdao repeatedly rebuked him before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner of military affairs Cao Liyong abused his power and acted arrogantly; Zongdao repeatedly confronted him before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 自貴戚用事者皆憚之，目為“魚頭參政”，因其姓，且言骨鯁如魚頭也。

translations.literal: From the noble clans to those wielding power, all feared him, and they called him "Fish-head Vice Councilor"—because of his surname Lu (fish) and because they said his bones were as stiff as a fish head.
translations.idiomatic: From the imperial kin to the powerful at court, all feared him. They nicknamed him "Fish-head Vice Councilor"—a play on his surname Lu, meaning fish, and a remark that his backbone was as stiff as a fish head.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書禮部侍郎、祥源觀使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to vice minister of rites in the Ministry of Revenue and commissioner of Xiangyuan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to vice minister of rites and made commissioner of Xiangyuan Temple.

sentences.zh: 在政府七年，務抑僥幸，不以名器私人。

translations.literal: In the government for seven years, he strove to restrain favor-seeking and did not bestow offices and honors on private persons.
translations.idiomatic: During seven years in the central government he worked to curb favoritism and refused to hand out offices and honors to private connections.

sentences.zh: 疾劇，帝臨問，賜白金三千兩。

translations.literal: When his illness grew severe, the emperor visited him in person and bestowed three thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave, the emperor visited him in person and granted three thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 既卒，皇太后臨奠之，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: After he died, the empress dowager came in person to offer mourning sacrifices and he was posthumously made minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the empress dowager came in person to mourn him, and he was posthumously made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 宗道為人剛正，疾惡少容，遇事敢言，不為小謹。

translations.literal: Zongdao was upright and stern, hated evil and had little tolerance, dared speak on affairs, and was not meticulous in small matters.
translations.idiomatic: Zongdao was upright and stern, intolerant of wrongdoing, and spoke boldly without fussing over minor proprieties.

sentences.zh: 為諭德時，居近酒肆，嘗微行就飲肆中，偶真宗亟召，使者及門久之，宗道方自酒肆來。

translations.literal: When he was tutor, he lived near a wine shop and once went in disguise to drink there. By chance Emperor Zhenzong urgently summoned him; the messenger reached his door and waited a long time before Zongdao came back from the wine shop.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as tutor he lived near a tavern and once went there in plain clothes to drink. Emperor Zhenzong happened to summon him urgently; the messenger waited at his door a long time before Zongdao returned from the tavern.

sentences.zh: 使者先入，約曰：“即上怪公來遲，何以為對？”

translations.literal: The messenger entered first and arranged with him, saying: "If His Majesty wonders why you are late, what shall we say in reply?"
translations.idiomatic: The messenger went in ahead of him and said: "If His Majesty asks why you are late, what shall we tell him?"

sentences.zh: 宗道曰：“第以實言之。”

translations.literal: Zongdao said: "Simply tell the truth."
translations.idiomatic: Zongdao said: "Just tell the truth."

sentences.zh: 使者曰：“然則公當得罪。”

translations.literal: The messenger said: "Then you will surely be punished."
translations.idiomatic: The messenger said: "Then you will surely be punished."

sentences.zh: 曰：“飲酒，人之常情；

translations.literal: He said: "Drinking wine is a human constant;
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Drinking is human nature;

sentences.zh: 欺君，臣子之大罪也。”

translations.literal: deceiving the ruler is a minister's great crime."
translations.idiomatic: deceiving one's sovereign is a minister's gravest offense."

sentences.zh: 真宗果問，使者具以宗道所言對。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong indeed asked, and the messenger reported Zongdao's words in full.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong did ask, the messenger repeated Zongdao's words exactly.

sentences.zh: 帝詰之，宗道謝曰：“有故人自鄉里來，臣家貧無杯盤，故就酒家飲。”

translations.literal: The emperor questioned him, and Zongdao apologized, saying: "An old friend came from my home district; my household is poor and has no cups and dishes, so I went to a wine shop to drink."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him further, and Zongdao explained: "An old friend had arrived from my home district. My household is poor and had no proper dishes, so I went to a tavern to entertain him."

sentences.zh: 帝以為忠實可大用，嘗以語太后，太后臨朝，遂大用之。

translations.literal: The emperor considered him loyal and honest and fit for great employment; he once spoke of this to the empress, and when the empress held court she greatly employed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him loyal and honest and fit for high office. He once told the empress about the incident, and when she later held court she relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 初，太常議諡曰剛簡，復改為肅簡。

translations.literal: At first the Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous title Gangjian (Steadfast and Simple), then changed it to Sujian (Solemn and Simple).
translations.idiomatic: At first the Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous title Gangjian (Steadfast and Simple), then changed it to Sujian (Solemn and Simple).

sentences.zh: 議者以為“肅”不若“剛”為得其實云。

translations.literal: Discussants held that "solemn" was not as true to the facts as "steadfast."
translations.idiomatic: Commentators felt that "solemn" did not capture his character as well as "steadfast" did.

sentences.zh: 薛奎，字宿藝，絳州正平人。

translations.literal: Xue Kui, styled Suyi, was a native of Zhengping in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Kui, whose courtesy name was Suyi, came from Zhengping in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父化光，善數術，嘗以平晉策幹太宗行在，召見不用，罷歸。

translations.literal: His father Huaguang was skilled in numerology and once presented a strategy for pacifying Jin at the emperor's traveling camp of Emperor Taizong; summoned and not employed, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huaguang was skilled in numerology and once offered Taizong a plan for pacifying Jin at the emperor's field headquarters; summoned but not employed, he went home.

sentences.zh: 適奎始生，撫其首曰：“是子必至公輔。”

translations.literal: Just as Kui was born, he stroked the child's head and said: "This boy will surely reach the rank of chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Just as Kui was born, he stroked the infant's head and said: "This child will surely rise to chief minister."

sentences.zh: 奎舉進士，為州第一，乃推與裏人王嚴，而處嚴下。

translations.literal: Kui passed the jinshi examination and ranked first in the prefecture, yet yielded the place to his fellow townsman Wang Yan and placed himself below Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Kui took the jinshi examination and ranked first in the prefecture, yet yielded first place to his fellow townsman Wang Yan and placed himself below him.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，為隰州軍事推官。

translations.literal: Having passed the jinshi examination, he became military judicial officer of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he became military judicial officer of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 州民常聚博僧舍，一日，盜殺寺奴取財去，博者適至，血偶涴衣，邏卒捕送州，考訊誣伏。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture often gathered to gamble in a Buddhist monastery. One day a thief killed a temple slave and took the goods away; gamblers happened to arrive, and blood happened to stain their clothes. Patrol soldiers seized and sent them to the prefecture; under interrogation they falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture often gambled in a Buddhist monastery. One day a thief killed a temple servant and made off with the goods. Gamblers arrived just then, and blood happened to stain their clothes. Patrolmen seized them and sent them to the prefecture, where interrogation forced false confessions.

sentences.zh: 奎獨疑之，白州緩其獄，後果得殺人者。

translations.literal: Kui alone doubted the case, reported to the prefecture to slow the trial, and later indeed obtained the real murderer.
translations.idiomatic: Kui alone doubted the case, persuaded the prefect to delay judgment, and later found the real killer.

sentences.zh: 徙儀州推官，嘗部丁夫運糧至鹽州，會久雨，粟麥漬腐，奎白轉運盧之翰，請縱民還州而償所失。

translations.literal: Transferred to judicial officer of Yizhou, he once led corvée laborers transporting grain to Yanzhou. Prolonged rain caused the grain and wheat to soak and rot. Kui reported to the transport commissioner Lu Zhihan, requesting to release the people back to the prefecture while compensating the loss.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to judicial officer of Yizhou, he once led corvée laborers hauling grain to Yanzhou. After long rains the grain and wheat rotted. Kui reported to transport commissioner Lu Zhihan and asked to send the laborers home while making good the loss.

sentences.zh: 之翰怒，欲劾奏之。

translations.literal: Zhihan was angry and wished to memorialize and impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihan was angry and wanted to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 奎徐曰：“用兵久，人疲轉餉，今幸兵食有餘，安用此陳腐以困民哉！”

translations.literal: Kui said calmly: "The army has been employed a long time and the people are weary of transporting provisions. Now fortunately military food is abundant—why use this stale grain to trouble the people!"
translations.idiomatic: Kui said calmly: "The army has been at war for years and the people are exhausted hauling supplies. We are fortunate that military stores are ample—why trouble them with rotten grain?"

sentences.zh: 之翰意解，凡民所失，悉奏除之。

translations.literal: Zhihan's mind was eased, and all the people's losses were memorialized for remission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihan relented, and all losses borne by the people were memorialized for remission.

sentences.zh: 改大理寺丞、知莆田縣。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Putian County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Putian County.

sentences.zh: 請蠲南閩時稅鹹魚、蒲草錢。

translations.literal: He requested remission of the wartime taxes on salted fish and sedge in southern Min.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to abolish the wartime taxes on salted fish and sedge grass in southern Fujian.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中丞、知長水縣，徙知永州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director in the palace service and magistrate of Changshui County, then moved to magistrate of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the palace service and magistrate of Changshui County, then transferred to Yongzhou as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 州有錢監，歲調兵三百人采鐵，而歲入不償費。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a mint, each year drafting three hundred soldiers to mine iron, yet annual revenue did not cover expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had a mint that each year drafted three hundred soldiers to mine iron, yet annual revenue did not cover the cost.

sentences.zh: 奎奏聽民自采，而所輸輒倍之。

translations.literal: Kui memorialized to allow the people to mine on their own, and what they delivered promptly doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Kui memorialized to let the people mine on their own, and their deliveries promptly doubled.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 向敏中薦為殿中侍御史，出為陝西轉運使。

translations.literal: Xiang Minzhong recommended him as palace censor and he went out as Shaanxi transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Minzhong recommended him as palace censor, and he went out as Shaanxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 趙德明言延州蕃落侵其地黑林平，下詔按驗。

translations.literal: Zhao Deming said the Tangut tribes at Yanzhou had invaded his territory at Heilinping; an edict ordered investigation and verification.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Deming claimed that Tangut tribes at Yanzhou had encroached on his territory at Heilinping, and the court ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 奎閱郡籍，德明嘗假道黑林平，移文錄示之，德明遂伏。

translations.literal: Kui examined the prefectural records; Deming had once borrowed passage through Heilinping, and Kui sent an official document with the record to show him; Deming thereupon submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Kui examined the prefectural records and found that Deming had once borrowed passage through Heilinping. He sent an official note with the record attached, and Deming at once backed down.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐失舉免。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed for a failure in recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed for a faulty recommendation.

sentences.zh: 數月，起通判陝州，改尚書戶部員外郎、淮南轉運副使，遷江、淮制置發運使。

translations.literal: Several months later he was recalled as supervisory commissioner of Shaanzhou, changed to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue in the Secretariat, vice transport commissioner of Huainan, and transferred to commissioner for river and Huai transport and grain distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was recalled as supervisory commissioner of Shaanzhou, made vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, vice transport commissioner of Huainan, then commissioner for Jiang-Huai transport and grain distribution.

sentences.zh: 疏漕河、廢三堰以便餉運，進吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He dredged the canal transport river and abolished three weirs to facilitate supply transport, and was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the canal and abolished three weirs to ease supply transport, and was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 父喪，奪哀，擢三司戶部副使。

translations.literal: When his father died he was recalled from mourning and promoted to vice commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue in the Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he was recalled from mourning and made vice commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue in the Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 與使李士衡爭論事，改戶部郎中、直昭文館、知延州。

translations.literal: He disputed affairs with commissioner Li Shiheng and was changed to director in the Ministry of Revenue, direct appointee of the Zhaowen Pavilion, and prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled with commissioner Li Shiheng over policy and was reassigned as director in the Ministry of Revenue, direct appointee of the Zhaowen Pavilion, and prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 趙元昊每遣吏至京師請奉予，吏因市禁物，隱關算為奸利，奎廉得狀，請留蜀道縑帛於關中，轉致給之。

translations.literal: Zhao Yuanhao each year sent officials to the capital to request stipends; the officials used the occasion to buy forbidden goods and concealed customs duties for illicit profit. Kui investigated and obtained the facts, requesting to retain Shu Road silk goods in Guanzhong and forward them for delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Zhao Yuanhao sent officials to the capital to request stipends; they bought forbidden goods and evaded customs duties for illicit profit. Kui investigated, obtained proof, and asked to keep Shu Road silk goods in Guanzhong and forward them as payment.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部，擢龍圖閣待制、權知開封府。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, he was promoted to awaiting academician of the Longtu Pavilion and acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, he was promoted to awaiting academician of the Longtu Pavilion and acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 為政嚴敏，擊斷無所貸，帝益加重。

translations.literal: In governance he was strict and keen, punishing without leniency, and the emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was strict and decisive, punishing without mercy, and the emperor valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，還，遷右諫議大夫、權御史中丞。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to the Khitan, on his return he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Counselor and acting censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Sent as envoy to the Khitan, he returned to become Right Remonstrance Counselor and acting censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 上疏論擇人、求治、崇節儉、屏聲色，凡十數事。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial discussing selection of men, pursuit of good order, esteem for frugality, and rejection of music and beauty—more than ten matters in all.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on choosing men, pursuing good government, honoring frugality, and rejecting music and sensual pleasure—more than ten topics in all.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后稱制，契丹使蕭從順請見太后，且言南使至契丹者皆見太后，而契丹使來乃不得見。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian held power, the Khitan envoy Xiao Congshun requested audience with the empress and said that southern envoys to the Khitan all saw the empress, yet Khitan envoys coming here could not see her.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian held power, the Khitan envoy Xiao Congshun asked to see the empress and complained that southern envoys to the Khitan all saw the empress while Khitan envoys here could not.

sentences.zh: 奎時館伴，折之曰：“皇太后垂簾聽政，雖本朝群臣，亦未嘗見也。”

translations.literal: Kui was then hosting the envoy and rebuked him, saying: "The empress dowager holds the curtain and hears government; even ministers of this court have never seen her."
translations.idiomatic: Kui was then hosting the envoy and rebuked him: "The empress dowager rules from behind the curtain. Even our own ministers have never seen her."

sentences.zh: 從順乃已。

translations.literal: Congshun then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Congshun then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 或讒云奎漏禁中語，改授集賢院學士、知并州，改秦州。

translations.literal: Some slandered that Kui had leaked palace secrets; he was reassigned academician of the Jixian Academy and prefect of Bingzhou, then changed to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Some slandered that he had leaked palace secrets. He was reassigned academician of the Jixian Academy and prefect of Bingzhou, then moved to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 州宿重兵，經費常不足，奎務為儉約，教民水耕，謹商算。

translations.literal: The prefecture long housed heavy troops and funds were often insufficient; Kui strove for economy, taught the people wet-field farming, and kept strict commercial accounts.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture long housed heavy garrisons and funds were often short; Kui practiced economy, taught wet-field farming, and kept strict commercial accounts.

sentences.zh: 歲中積粟三百萬，征算餘三千萬，核民隱田數千頃，得芻粟十餘萬。

translations.literal: Within the year he accumulated three million bushels of grain, three million in tax surplus, verified several thousand qing of concealed private fields, and obtained more than a hundred thousand bundles of fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he accumulated three million bushels of grain, thirty million in tax surplus, uncovered several thousand qing of concealed private fields, and obtained more than a hundred thousand bundles of fodder.

sentences.zh: 加樞密直學士、知益州。

translations.literal: He was made associate academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made associate academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 秦民與夷落數千人列奎治狀，請留，璽書褒諭，不許。

translations.literal: Several thousand Qin people together with tribal settlements listed Kui's achievements in governance and asked that he remain; an imperial letter praised him but did not grant the request.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Qin people and tribal groups petitioned listing his achievements and asking that he stay; an imperial letter praised him but did not allow it.

sentences.zh: 成都民婦訟其子不孝，詰之，乃曰：“貧無以為養。”

translations.literal: A Chengdu woman sued her son for unfilial conduct; on questioning him he said: "We are poor and have no means to support her."
translations.idiomatic: A Chengdu woman sued her son for unfilial conduct. When questioned, the son said: "We are too poor to support her properly."

sentences.zh: 奎出俸錢與之，戒曰：“若復失養，吾不貸汝矣！”

translations.literal: Kui gave him salary money and warned: "If you fail in support again, I shall not spare you!"
translations.idiomatic: Kui gave him money from his own salary and warned: "If you neglect her again, I will not spare you!"

sentences.zh: 其母子遂如初。

translations.literal: Mother and son thereupon returned to their former ways.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and son then lived together as before.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜燕，有戍卒殺人，人皆奔走，奎密遣捕殺之，坐客莫有知者。

translations.literal: Once at a night banquet a garrison soldier killed someone; everyone fled in panic. Kui secretly sent men to seize and kill him, and none of the seated guests knew.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a night banquet a garrison soldier killed someone and guests fled in panic. Kui secretly sent men to seize and execute him, and none of the guests knew.

sentences.zh: 臨事持重明決，多此類也。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he was weighty, clear, and decisive—many cases were like this.
translations.idiomatic: In handling affairs he was steady, clear, and decisive—many cases were like this.

sentences.zh: 召為龍圖閣學士、權三司使，遂參知政事。

translations.literal: He was summoned as academician of the Longtu Pavilion and acting commissioner of the Finance Commission, then became Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as academician of the Longtu Pavilion and acting commissioner of the Finance Commission, then made vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 帝諭曰：“先帝嘗以為卿可任，今用卿，先帝意也。”

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him: "The late emperor once thought you fit for employment; in using you now, it is the late emperor's intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "The late emperor once judged you fit for high office. In appointing you now, I follow his intent."

sentences.zh: 俄遷給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂輔臣曰：“臣事君鮮有克終者。”

translations.literal: The emperor once said to the chief ministers: "Ministers serving their rulers rarely succeed to the end."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told his chief ministers: "Few ministers who serve their sovereign manage to finish what they begin."

sentences.zh: 奎曰：“保終之道，匪獨臣不然也。”

translations.literal: Kui said: "The way to preserve one's end is not something only ministers fail at."
translations.idiomatic: Kui replied: "The path to a worthy ending is not something only ministers fail to walk."

sentences.zh: 曆數唐開元、天寶時事以對，帝然之。

translations.literal: He enumerated affairs of the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns of Tang in reply, and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: He answered by recounting events from the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns of Tang, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of rites in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 太后謁太廟，欲被服天子袞冕，奎曰：“必御此，若何為拜？”

translations.literal: When the empress dowager visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple she wished to wear the emperor's dragon robe and coronet. Kui said: "If you must wear this, how can you perform the bows?"
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple she wished to wear the emperor's dragon robe and coronet. Kui said: "If you wear these, how can you perform the ritual bows?"

sentences.zh: 力陳其不可，終不見聽。

translations.literal: He strongly stated it was impossible, but in the end was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He argued forcefully against it, but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 及太后崩，帝見左右泣曰：“太后疾不能言，猶數引其衣若有所屬，何也？”

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, the emperor saw those beside him weeping and said: "The empress dowager's illness left her unable to speak, yet she repeatedly pulled at her garment as if indicating something—what was it?"
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager died, the emperor saw attendants weeping and said: "In her illness she could not speak, yet she kept pulling at her robe as if to indicate something. What did she mean?"

sentences.zh: 奎曰：“其在袞冕也。

translations.literal: Kui said: "It concerned the dragon robe and coronet.
translations.idiomatic: Kui said: "It was about the dragon robe and coronet.

sentences.zh: 服之豈可見先帝於地下！”

translations.literal: How could she meet the late emperor underground wearing them!"
translations.idiomatic: How could she face the late emperor in the afterlife wearing them!"

sentences.zh: 帝悟，卒以后服斂。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and in the end had her buried in empress's garb.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and had her buried in proper empress's attire.

sentences.zh: 因上言請逐內侍羅崇勳等。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial requesting expulsion of the inner attendant Luo Chongxun and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized asking that the inner attendant Luo Chongxun and others be removed.

sentences.zh: 時二府大臣多罷去，奎得喘疾，數辭位，罷為戶部侍郎、資政殿學士、判尚書都省。

translations.literal: At the time many chief ministers of the two councils had been dismissed; Kui contracted asthma and repeatedly asked to resign, and was dismissed as vice minister of revenue, academician of the Zizheng Hall, and director of the Secretariat's general office.
translations.idiomatic: Many chief ministers of the two councils had already been dismissed. Kui developed asthma, repeatedly asked to resign, and was relieved as vice minister of revenue, academician of the Zizheng Hall, and director of the Secretariat's general office.

sentences.zh: 帝手書禁方賜之，小間，入見。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote a forbidden prescription and bestowed it; after a short while he entered for audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote out a secret medical prescription for him and, a little later, received him in audience.

sentences.zh: 疾尋作，卒，贈兵部尚書，諡簡肅。

translations.literal: His illness soon broke out and he died; he was posthumously made minister of war with the posthumous title Jiansu (Simple and Solemn).
translations.idiomatic: His illness soon worsened and he died. He was posthumously made minister of war with the posthumous title Jiansu (Simple and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 奎性剛不苟合，遇事敢言，真宗時數宴大臣，至有沾醉者。

translations.literal: Kui's nature was stern and he would not compromise; on affairs he dared speak out. In Emperor Zhenzong's time he often banqueted the chief ministers, and some even became drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was stern and uncompromising and spoke boldly on public affairs. Under Zhenzong the court often banqueted chief ministers until some were visibly drunk.

sentences.zh: 奎諫曰：“陛下即位之初，勵精萬幾而簡宴幸。

translations.literal: Kui remonstrated: "When Your Majesty first took the throne, you strove in the myriad affairs of state and kept banquets few.
translations.idiomatic: Kui remonstrated: "When Your Majesty first took the throne, you devoted yourself to governance and kept feasts few.

sentences.zh: 今天下誠無事，而宴樂無度，大臣數被酒無威儀，非所以重朝廷也。”

translations.literal: Now though the realm is truly without affairs, yet feasting and pleasure are without limit and the chief ministers are often drunk without dignity—this is not the way to honor the court."
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm may be at peace, yet feasting knows no limit and ministers often appear before you drunk and undignified. That is no way to honor the court."

sentences.zh: 真宗善其言。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong approved his words.

sentences.zh: 及參政事，謀議無所避。

translations.literal: When he joined the government, in counsel and deliberation he avoided nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the central government he spoke his mind without holding back.

sentences.zh: 能知人，范仲淹、龐籍、明鎬自為吏部選人，皆以公輔許之。

translations.literal: He could know men; Fan Zhongyan, Pang Ji, and Ming Hao, from the time they were selected by the Ministry of Personnel, he all promised would reach chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for judging men. Fan Zhongyan, Pang Ji, and Ming Hao were still only candidates in the Ministry of Personnel when he already predicted they would reach the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 無子，以從子為嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, he took a younger clansman's son as heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son and adopted a younger clansman's child as heir.

sentences.zh: 王曙，字晦叔，隋東皋子績之後。

translations.literal: Wang Shu, styled Huishu, was a descendant of Wang Ji, the Eastern Gaozi of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, whose courtesy name was Huishu, was descended from Wang Ji, the Eastern Gaozi of Sui.

sentences.zh: 世居河汾，後為河南人。

translations.literal: His family long dwelt in the Fen and Fen region and later became people of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived along the Fen River and later became residents of Henan.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，再調定國軍節度推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was twice transferred as military judicial officer of the Dingguo Army command.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served twice as military judicial officer under the Dingguo Army command.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，舉賢良方正科，策入等，遷秘書省著作佐郎、知定海縣。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era he was recommended in the erudite and upright category; his policy essay entered the top grade and he was transferred to assistant in the Secretariat's works office and magistrate of Dinghai County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era he entered the erudite and upright examination; his policy essay ranked in the top grade and he was made assistant in the Secretariat's works office and magistrate of Dinghai County.

sentences.zh: 還，為群牧判官，考集古今馬政，為《群牧故事》六卷，上之。

translations.literal: On his return he was herds judge of the Herds Office, examined and collected ancient and modern horse administration, compiled six fascicles of Herds Office Stories, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he became herds judge of the Herds Office, compiled ancient and modern records of horse administration into six fascicles titled Herds Office Stories, and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 遷太常丞、判三司憑由理欠司。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and director of the Finance Commission's credentials and arrears office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and director of the Finance Commission's credentials and arrears office.

sentences.zh: 坐舉進士失實，降監盧州茶稅，再遷尚書工部員外郎、龍圖閣待制。

translations.literal: For recommending a jinshi candidate inaccurately he was demoted to supervisor of Luzhou tea tax, then again transferred to vice director of works in the Ministry of Revenue and awaiting academician of the Longtu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Because a jinshi candidate he recommended was found inaccurate, he was demoted to supervisor of Luzhou tea tax, then restored as vice director of works and awaiting academician of the Longtu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 以右諫議大夫為河北轉運使，坐部吏受賕，降知壽州。

translations.literal: As Right Remonstrance Counselor he was made Hebei transport commissioner; for his subordinate officials accepting bribes he was demoted to prefect of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Remonstrance Counselor he became Hebei transport commissioner, but was demoted to prefect of Shouzhou when subordinates accepted bribes.

sentences.zh: 徙淮南轉運使，勾當三班院，權知開封府。

translations.literal: Transferred to Huainan transport commissioner, he handled the Third Class Bureau and acted as prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Huainan transport commissioner, oversaw the Third Class Bureau, and acted as prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 以樞密直學士知益州。

translations.literal: As associate academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs he was made prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As associate academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs he was made prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 繩盜以峻法，多致之死。

translations.literal: He restrained bandits with severe law and often brought them to death.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued bandits with harsh laws and often had them executed.

sentences.zh: 有卒夜告其軍將亂，立辨其偽，斬之。

translations.literal: A soldier reported at night that his commander was plotting rebellion; he promptly judged it false and executed the informant.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier reported at night that his commander was plotting rebellion; Shu immediately judged the report false and executed the informant.

sentences.zh: 蜀人比之張詠，號“前張後王”。

translations.literal: The people of Shu compared him to Zhang Yong and called him "Zhang before, Wang after."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu compared him to Zhang Yong and called him "Zhang before, Wang after."

sentences.zh: 入為給事中。

translations.literal: He entered court as Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為皇太子，與李迪同選兼賓客，復坐貢舉失實，黜官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong was crown prince, he was chosen together with Li Di as concurrent tutors; again for errors in the tribute examination he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was crown prince, he and Li Di were chosen as his tutors. He was dismissed again for errors in the tribute examination.

sentences.zh: 復為給事中兼群牧使。

translations.literal: He was restored as Supervising Secretary and concurrent herds commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Supervising Secretary and concurrent herds commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其妻，寇準女也。

translations.literal: His wife was the daughter of Kou Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Kou Zhun's daughter.

sentences.zh: 準罷相且貶，曙亦降知汝州。

translations.literal: When Zhun was dismissed from the chancellorship and also demoted, Shu was also demoted to prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Kou Zhun was dismissed and demoted, Shu was demoted to prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 準再貶，曙亦貶郢州團練副使。

translations.literal: When Zhun was demoted again, Shu was also demoted to military training vice commissioner of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Kou Zhun was demoted again, Shu was demoted to military training vice commissioner of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 起為光祿卿、知襄州，又徙汝州。

translations.literal: He was recalled as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Xiangzhou, then moved to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Xiangzhou, then moved to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 復給事中、知潞州。

translations.literal: Restored as Supervising Secretary, he was made prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Restored as Supervising Secretary, he became prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 州有殺人者，獄已具，曙獨疑之。

translations.literal: In the prefecture there was a murder case already concluded; Shu alone doubted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefecture a murder case had already been closed, but Shu alone doubted it.

sentences.zh: 既而提點刑獄杜衍至，事果辨。

translations.literal: Before long the judicial intendant Du Yan arrived and the matter was indeed clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon judicial intendant Du Yan arrived and the matter was indeed cleared.

sentences.zh: 曙為作《辨獄記》以戒官吏。

translations.literal: Shu wrote Discerning Prison Cases as a warning to officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shu wrote Discerning Prison Cases to warn officials against such errors.

sentences.zh: 徙河南府、永興軍，召為御史中丞兼理檢使，理檢置使自此始。

translations.literal: Transferred to Henan prefecture and the Yongxing Army, he was summoned as censor-in-chief and concurrent inspection commissioner; the establishment of the inspection commissioner began here.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Henan prefecture and the Yongxing Army, he was summoned as censor-in-chief and concurrent inspection commissioner—the post of inspection commissioner began with him.

sentences.zh: 玉清昭應宮災，繫守衛者御史獄。

translations.literal: When the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace burned, the guards were imprisoned in the censor's jail.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace burned, the guards were imprisoned in the censor's jail.

sentences.zh: 曙恐朝廷議修復，上言：“昔魯桓、僖宮災，孔子以為桓、僖親盡當毀者也。

translations.literal: Shu feared the court would discuss rebuilding and submitted a memorial: "In former times when the palaces of Duke Huan and Duke Xi of Lu burned, Confucius held that Huan and Xi had exhausted their kin ties and the palaces ought to be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the court would discuss rebuilding, Shu memorialized: "When the palaces of Duke Huan and Duke Xi of Lu burned, Confucius held that their kin ties were exhausted and the palaces ought to be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 遼東高廟及高園便殿災，董仲舒以為高廟不當居陵旁，故災。

translations.literal: When the Gaomiao and Gaoyuan side hall in Liaodong burned, Dong Zhongshu held that the Gaomiao ought not stand beside the tomb, hence the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaomiao and Gaoyuan side hall in Liaodong burned, Dong Zhongshu held that the Gaomiao should not stand beside the tomb, hence the disaster.

sentences.zh: 魏崇華殿災，高堂隆以壹榭宮室為戒，宜罷之勿治，文帝不聽，明年，復災。

translations.literal: When the Chonghua Hall of Wei burned, Gao Tanglong took a single pavilion as a warning and advised stopping repair; Emperor Wen did not listen, and the next year it burned again.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei's Chonghua Hall burned, Gao Tanglong warned against extravagant palaces and advised halting repairs; Emperor Wen did not listen, and the next year it burned again.

sentences.zh: 今所建宮非應經義，災變之來若有警者。

translations.literal: The palace now built does not accord with canonical principle; the coming of disaster and anomaly seems to carry a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The palace now proposed does not accord with canonical principle; the disaster seems to carry a warning.

sentences.zh: 願除其地，罷諸禱祠，以應天變。”

translations.literal: I wish the site cleared and all prayer shrines abolished to respond to Heaven's warning."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the site be cleared and prayer shrines abolished to answer Heaven's warning."

sentences.zh: 仁宗與太后感悟，遂減守衛者罪。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong and the empress were moved and thereupon reduced the guards' punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong and the empress were moved and reduced the guards' punishment.

sentences.zh: 已而詔以不復繕修諭天下。

translations.literal: Before long an edict announced to the realm that repair would not be undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict announced throughout the realm that the palace would not be rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 又請三品以上立家廟，復唐舊制。

translations.literal: He also requested that officials of the third rank and above establish family temples, restoring the Tang old system.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that officials of the third rank and above establish family temples, restoring the Tang system.

sentences.zh: 以尚書工部侍郎參知政事。

translations.literal: As vice minister of works in the Ministry of Revenue he became Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: As vice minister of works he became vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 以疾請罷，改戶部侍郎、資政殿學士、知陝州，徙河陽。

translations.literal: Illness led him to request dismissal; he was changed to vice minister of revenue, academician of the Zizheng Hall, and prefect of Shaanzhou, then moved to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led him to request dismissal; he was made vice minister of revenue, academician of the Zizheng Hall, and prefect of Shaanzhou, then moved to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 再知河南府，遷吏部。

translations.literal: Again made prefect of Henan, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Again made prefect of Henan, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 召為樞密使，拜同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Summoned as commissioner of military affairs, he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Tongzhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi rank.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as commissioner of military affairs, he was appointed grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 逾月，首發疽，卒。

translations.literal: After more than a month an abscess broke out first and he died.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month an abscess broke out and he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太保、中書令，諡文康。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Guardian and Grand Preceptor of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Wenkang (Cultured and Tranquil).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian and Grand Preceptor of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Wenkang (Cultured and Tranquil).

sentences.zh: 曙方嚴簡重，有大臣體，居官深自抑損。

translations.literal: Shu was stern, simple, and weighty, with the bearing of a great minister; in office he deeply restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was stern, dignified, and weighty, with the bearing of a great minister, and deeply restrained himself in office.

sentences.zh: 喜浮圖法，齋居蔬食，泊如也。

translations.literal: He favored Buddhist law, kept vegetarian fasts at home, and was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He favored Buddhist practice, kept vegetarian fasts at home, and lived quietly.

sentences.zh: 初，錢惟演留守西京，歐陽修、尹洙為官屬。

translations.literal: At first Qian Weiyan was left to guard the western capital; Ouyang Xiu and Yin Zhu were his subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: At first Qian Weiyan guarded the western capital; Ouyang Xiu and Yin Zhu served under him.

sentences.zh: 修等頗遊宴，曙後至，嘗厲色戒修等曰：“諸君縱酒過度，獨不知寇萊公晚年之禍邪！”

translations.literal: Xiu and the others often feasted and drank excessively; Shu arrived later and once sternly warned Xiu and the others: "You all drink to excess—do you alone not know the late fate of Minister Kou in his old age?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and the others often feasted excessively. When Shu arrived later he sternly warned them: "You drink without limit—have you forgotten Minister Kou's fate in his old age?"

sentences.zh: 修起對曰：“以修聞之，萊公正坐老而不知止爾！”

translations.literal: Xiu rose and replied: "As I have heard, Minister Kou was ruined precisely because in old age he did not know when to stop!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu rose and replied: "As I understand it, Minister Kou was ruined because in old age he did not know when to stop!"

sentences.zh: 曙默然，終不怒。

translations.literal: Shu was silent and in the end was not angry.
translations.idiomatic: Shu fell silent and never grew angry.

sentences.zh: 及為樞密使，首薦修等，置之館閣。

translations.literal: When he became commissioner of military affairs he first recommended Xiu and the others and placed them in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When he became commissioner of military affairs he first recommended Xiu and the others and placed them in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 有集四十卷，《周書音訓》十二卷，《唐書備問》三卷，《莊子旨歸》三篇，《列子旨歸》一篇，《戴鬥奉使錄》二卷，集《兩漢詔議》四十卷。

translations.literal: He had forty fascicles of collected works, twelve fascicles of Pronunciation of the Zhou History, three fascicles of Questions on the Tang History, three chapters of The Meaning of Zhuangzi, one chapter of The Meaning of Liezi, two fascicles of Record of the Dai Dou Embassy, and forty fascicles collecting edicts of the two Han dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to forty fascicles; he also wrote twelve fascicles on Zhou pronunciation, three on questions about the Tang History, essays on Zhuangzi and Liezi, two fascicles on the Dai Dou embassy, and forty fascicles of edicts from the two Han dynasties.

sentences.zh: 子益恭、益柔。

translations.literal: His sons were Yigong and Yirou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yigong and Yirou.

sentences.zh: 益恭字達夫，以蔭為衛尉寺丞。

translations.literal: Yigong, styled Dafu, entered office through yin privilege as vice director of the Court of Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong, whose courtesy name was Dafu, entered office through yin privilege as vice director of the Court of Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 性恬淡，慕唐王龜之為人，數解官就養。

translations.literal: His nature was tranquil; he admired Tang Wang Guizhi and several times resigned office to care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Tranquil by nature, he admired Tang Wang Guizhi and several times resigned to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 曙參知政事，治第西京，益恭勸曙引年謝事，曙不果去。

translations.literal: When Shu became vice grand councilor he built a residence in the western capital; Yigong urged Shu to retire on grounds of age, but Shu did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu became vice grand councilor he built a residence in the western capital; Yigong urged him to retire on grounds of age, but Shu did not leave.

sentences.zh: 終父喪，遂以尚書司門員外郎致仕，間與浮圖、隱者出遊，洛陽名園山水，無不至也。

translations.literal: After his father's mourning ended he retired as vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's gate office, and from time to time traveled with Buddhists and recluses; famous gardens, mountains, and rivers of Luoyang—none he did not visit.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning he retired as vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's gate office and often traveled with Buddhists and recluses through Luoyang's famous gardens, mountains, and rivers.

sentences.zh: 以子登朝，累遷司農少卿，卒。

translations.literal: Because his son entered court he was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Granaries and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his son entered court he was promoted repeatedly to vice director of the Court of Imperial Granaries and died.

translations.literal: 〈Son〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Son〉

sentences.zh: 益柔

translations.literal: Yirou
translations.idiomatic: Yirou

sentences.zh: 益柔字勝之。

translations.literal: Yirou, styled Shengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yirou, whose courtesy name was Shengzhi.

sentences.zh: 為人伉直尚氣，喜論天下事。

translations.literal: In person he was upright and spirited, fond of discussing affairs of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and high-spirited, he loved to discuss affairs of the realm.

sentences.zh: 用蔭至殿中丞。

translations.literal: Through yin privilege he reached palace director.
translations.idiomatic: Through yin privilege he rose to palace director.

sentences.zh: 元昊叛，上備邊選將之策。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao rebelled he submitted a strategy for selecting border generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao rebelled he submitted a strategy for choosing border generals.

sentences.zh: 杜衍、丁度宣撫河東，益柔寓書言：“河外兵餉無法，非易帥臣、轉運使不可。”

translations.literal: Du Yan and Ding Du were pacification commissioners of Hedong; Yirou sent a letter saying: "Beyond the river military provisions have no system—it cannot be remedied without changing the commander and transport commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: When Du Yan and Ding Du were pacification commissioners of Hedong, Yirou wrote: "Military supplies beyond the river have no proper system. The commander and transport commissioner must be changed."

sentences.zh: 因條其可任者。

translations.literal: He thereupon listed those fit for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He then listed men fit for the posts.

sentences.zh: 衍、度使還，以學術政事薦，知介丘縣。

translations.literal: When Yan and Du returned from their commission they recommended him for learning and governance, and he was made magistrate of Jieqiu County.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan and Du returned they recommended him for scholarship and governance, and he was made magistrate of Jieqiu County.

sentences.zh: 慶曆更用執政，異意者指為朋黨，仁宗下詔戒敕，益柔上書論辨，言尤切直。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era the ruling group was changed; those of different intent were called a faction; Emperor Renzong issued an edict of warning and admonition; Yirou submitted a memorial of argument, and his words were especially cutting and direct.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli reshuffle those of different views were called a faction. Renzong issued a warning edict; Yirou memorialized in rebuttal with especially sharp words.

sentences.zh: 尹洙與劉滬爭城水洛事，自涇原貶慶州。

translations.literal: Yin Zhu and Liu Hu disputed the Shuiluo fort affair; Zhu was demoted from Jingyuan to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhu and Liu Hu disputed the Shuiluo fort affair, and Zhu was demoted from Jingyuan to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 益柔訟之曰：“水洛一障耳，不足以拒賊。

translations.literal: Yirou pleaded on his behalf: "Shuiluo is only one barrier and insufficient to repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yirou pleaded for Zhu: "Shuiluo is only one outpost and cannot repel the enemy alone.

sentences.zh: 滬裨將，洙為將軍，以天子命呼之不至，戮之不為過；

translations.literal: Hu is a deputy general and Zhu a commanding general; for the Son of Heaven's order to summon him and he does not come, to execute him would not be excessive;
translations.idiomatic: Hu is a deputy and Zhu a commanding general. If the Son of Heaven summons him and he does not come, execution would not be excessive;

sentences.zh: 顧不敢專執之以聽命，是洙不伸將軍之職而上尊朝廷，未見其有罪也。”

translations.literal: yet he did not dare execute on his own authority but listened for orders—this is Zhu not exceeding a general's duty but honoring the court above; I do not see his crime."
translations.idiomatic: yet Zhu did not dare execute on his own but awaited orders—that is honoring the court, not exceeding a general's duty. I see no crime."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not listen.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹未識面，以館閣薦之，除集賢校理。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan had not met him but recommended him through the Hanlin Academy; he was made collator of the Jixian collection.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan, though he had not met him, recommended him through the Hanlin Academy and he was made collator of the Jixian collection.

sentences.zh: 預蘇舜欽奏邸會，醉作《傲歌》。

translations.literal: He took part in Su Shunqin's lodge gathering memorial and, drunk, composed Arrogant Song.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in Su Shunqin's lodge gathering memorial and, while drunk, composed Arrogant Song.

sentences.zh: 時諸人欲遂傾正黨，宰相章得象、晏殊不可否，參政賈昌朝陰主之，張方平、宋祁、王拱辰攻排不遺力，至列狀言益柔罪當誅。

translations.literal: At the time some wished to overturn the upright faction; Grand Councilor Zhang Dexiang and Yan Shu neither approved nor denied; Vice Councilor Jia Changchao backed them secretly; Zhang Fangping, Song Qi, and Wang Gongchen attacked without sparing effort, even submitting a joint memorial that Yirou's crime deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Some then sought to destroy the upright faction. Grand Councilor Zhang Dexiang and Yan Shu would neither approve nor deny; Vice Councilor Jia Changchao backed them secretly; Zhang Fangping, Song Qi, and Wang Gongchen attacked relentlessly, even memorializing that Yirou deserved death.

sentences.zh: 韓琦為帝言：“益柔狂語何足深計。

translations.literal: Han Qi said to the emperor: "Yirou's wild words are not worth deep concern.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi told the emperor: "Yirou's reckless words are not worth serious concern.

sentences.zh: 方平等皆陛下近臣，今西陲用兵，大事何限，一不為陛下論列，而同狀攻一王益柔，此其意可見矣。”

translations.literal: Fangping and the others are all Your Majesty's close ministers; now on the western border war is waged and great affairs are countless—yet they do not discuss them for Your Majesty but jointly attack one Wang Yirou; their intent can be seen."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fangping and the others are Your Majesty's close ministers. The western border is at war and great affairs abound, yet they discuss none of them and jointly attack one Wang Yirou. Their intent is plain."

sentences.zh: 帝感悟，但黜監復州酒。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and only demoted him to supervisor of Fuzhou wine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and only demoted him to supervisor of Fuzhou wine.

sentences.zh: 久之，為開封府推官、鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made Kaifeng judicial officer and salt-iron judge.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was made Kaifeng judicial officer and salt-iron judge.

sentences.zh: 凡中旨所需不應法式，有司迎合以求進者，悉論之不置。

translations.literal: Whenever central edicts required something not in proper form and offices curried favor to seek advancement, he discussed them all and would not let them stand.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever central edicts demanded something improper and offices curried favor to advance favorites, he blocked them all.

sentences.zh: 出為兩浙、京東西轉運使。

translations.literal: He went out as transport commissioner of the two Zhe and the two Jing circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as transport commissioner of the two Zhe and two Jing circuits.

sentences.zh: 上言：“今考課法區別長吏能否，必明有顯狀，顯狀必取其更置興作大利。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Today's examination law distinguishes the ability of chief officials and requires clear conspicuous signs; conspicuous signs must take their replacement's establishment of great profitable works.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Today's examination law judges chief officials only by conspicuous achievements, and conspicuous achievements mean major profitable projects by one's successor.

sentences.zh: 夫小政小善，積而不已，然後能成其大。

translations.literal: Small policies and small goods accumulated without cease can then accomplish the great.
translations.idiomatic: Yet small policies and small goods steadily accumulated can accomplish great things.

sentences.zh: 取其大而遺其細，將競利圖功，恐事之不舉者日多，而虛名無實之風日起。

translations.literal: Taking the great and abandoning the small, they will compete for profit and scheme for merit; I fear those whose affairs do not succeed will daily increase, and the wind of empty name without substance will daily rise.
translations.idiomatic: If we prize only grand projects and neglect small ones, officials will scramble for profit and credit. Failures will multiply and empty reputation without real achievement will spread.

sentences.zh: 願參以唐四善，兼取行實，列為三等。”

translations.literal: I wish to consult the Tang Four Goods, take conduct into account together, and arrange them in three grades."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we consult the Tang 'Four Goods,' weigh actual conduct, and rank officials in three grades."

sentences.zh: 不行。

translations.literal: It was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，入判度支審院。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining he entered to judge the Revenue Review Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xining reign he entered to judge the Revenue Review Court.

sentences.zh: 詔百官轉對，益柔言：“人君之難，莫大於辨邪正；

translations.literal: An edict ordered all officials to present rotating memorials; Yirou said: "For a ruler the greatest difficulty is distinguishing the wicked from the upright;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered rotating memorials from all officials. Yirou said: "A ruler's greatest difficulty is telling wicked from upright;

sentences.zh: 邪正之辨，莫大於置相。

translations.literal: the greatest difficulty in distinguishing wicked from upright lies in appointing a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: and the greatest difficulty in that lies in appointing a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 相之忠邪，百官之賢否也。

translations.literal: Whether the chancellor is loyal or wicked determines whether the hundred officials are worthy or not.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the chancellor is loyal or wicked determines whether the hundred officials are worthy or not.

sentences.zh: 若唐高宗之李義甫，明皇之李林甫，德宗之盧杞，憲宗之皇甫鎛，帝王之鑒也。

translations.literal: Such as Li Yifu of Emperor Gaozong of Tang, Li Linfu of Emperor Ming of Tang, Lu Qi of Emperor Dezong, and Huangfu Bo of Emperor Xian of Tang—the mirrors of emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu under Tang Gaozong, Li Linfu under Minghuang, Lu Qi under Dezong, Huangfu Bo under Xianzong—these are mirrors for emperors.

sentences.zh: 高宗、德宗之昏蒙，固無足論；

translations.literal: The benightedness of Gaozong and Dezong is truly not worth discussion;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong and Dezong were benighted and hardly worth discussion;

sentences.zh: 明皇、憲宗之聰明，乃蔽於二人如此。

translations.literal: yet Ming and Xian were intelligent and were still so blinded by two men.
translations.idiomatic: yet Minghuang and Xianzong were intelligent and still blinded by two men each.

sentences.zh: 以二人之庸，猶足以致禍，況誦六藝、挾才智以文致其奸說者哉！”

translations.literal: With the mediocrity of those two men they could still bring disaster—how much more those who recite the Six Classics and wield talent and intelligence to clothe their wicked doctrines!"
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre men could still bring disaster—how much more those who recite the classics and wield talent to dress up wicked doctrines!"

sentences.zh: 意蓋指王安石也。

translations.literal: His intent presumably pointed at Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: His intent plainly targeted Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: He judged the Ministry of Personnel's mobile selection office.
translations.idiomatic: He judged the Ministry of Personnel's mobile selection office.

sentences.zh: 舊制，選人當改京官，滿十人乃引見。

translations.literal: By old regulation, when candidates were to be changed to capital officials, ten had to be filled before presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, candidates advancing to capital office had to wait until ten were ready before presentation.

sentences.zh: 由是士多困滯，且遇舉者有故，輒不用。

translations.literal: Therefore scholars were often stalled in office, and when the recommender had some reason they were often not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars were often stalled, and when a recommender had some excuse they were often passed over.

sentences.zh: 益柔請才二人即引見，眾論翕然稱之。

translations.literal: Yirou requested that when two were talented they be presented at once; public discussion unanimously praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Yirou asked that two talented men be presented at once; public opinion warmly praised the change.

sentences.zh: 直舍人院、知制誥兼直學士院。

translations.literal: Direct appointee of the Drafting Office, drafter of edicts and concurrent direct academician of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was direct appointee of the Drafting Office, drafter of edicts, and concurrent direct academician of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 董氈遇明堂恩，中書熟狀加光祿大夫，而舊階已特進，益柔以聞。

translations.literal: Dong Zhan encountered the Bright Hall grace; the Secretariat's routine memorial added Grandee of Splendid Happiness, yet his old rank was already Special Advancement; Yirou reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhan received Bright Hall grace, the Secretariat's routine memorial added Grandee of Splendid Happiness though his old rank was already Special Advancement; Yirou reported the error.

sentences.zh: 帝謂中書曰：“非翰林，幾何不為羌夷所笑。”

translations.literal: The emperor said to the Secretariat: "Were it not for the Hanlin Academy, we would nearly have been laughed at by the tribal peoples."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the Secretariat: "Without the Hanlin Academy we would nearly have been mocked by the frontier tribes."

sentences.zh: 宰相怒其不申堂，用他事罷其兼直。

translations.literal: The chief minister was angry that he had not reported through the council hall and used another matter to dismiss his concurrent direct appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister was angry he had not reported through the council and used another matter to strip his concurrent academy post.

sentences.zh: 遷龍圖閣直學士、秘書監，知蔡揚亳州、江寧應天府。

translations.literal: Transferred to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and director of the palace library, and prefect of Cai, Yang, Bozhou, Jiangning, and Yingtian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was made direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and director of the palace library, and served as prefect of Cai, Yang, Bozhou, Jiangning, and Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 益柔少力學，通群書，為文日數千言。

translations.literal: Yirou from youth studied hard, mastered many books, and in writing produced several thousand characters a day.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yirou studied hard, mastered many books, and could write several thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 尹洙見之曰：“贍而不流，制而不窘，語淳而厲，氣壯而長，未可量也。”

translations.literal: Yin Zhu saw him and said: "Rich yet not diffuse, restrained yet not cramped, language pure yet stern, spirit strong yet sustained—he cannot yet be measured."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhu said of him: "Rich without overflowing, restrained without cramping, language pure yet stern, spirit strong yet sustained—his measure is not yet known."

sentences.zh: 時方以詩賦取士，益柔去不為。

translations.literal: At the time poetry and fu were used to select scholars; Yirou left and did not compose them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time scholars were chosen by poetry and fu; Yirou refused to compete on those terms.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹薦試館職，以其不善詞賦，乞試以策論，特聽之。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan recommended him for examination for academy office; because he was not skilled in lyric and fu, he begged to be tested by policy essays and was specially permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan recommended him for Hanlin examination; because he was weak in lyric and fu he asked to be tested on policy essays and was specially allowed.

sentences.zh: 司馬光嘗語人曰：“自吾為《資治通鑒》，人多欲求觀讀，未終一紙，已欠伸思睡。

translations.literal: Sima Guang once told people: "Since I wrote Comprehensive Mirror, many wish to borrow and read it; before finishing one sheet they already stretch and think of sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang once said: "Since I wrote Comprehensive Mirror, many ask to read it, but before finishing one page they stretch and want to sleep.

sentences.zh: 能閱之終篇者，惟王勝之耳。”

translations.literal: The only one who can read it to the end is Wang Shengzhi alone."
translations.idiomatic: The only one who can read it through is Wang Shengzhi."

sentences.zh: 其好學類此。

translations.literal: His love of learning was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His love of learning was of that sort.

sentences.zh: 蔡齊，字子思，其先洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Cai Qi, styled Zisi, his ancestors were people of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Qi, whose courtesy name was Zisi, came originally from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖綰，為萊州膠水令，因家焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Wan was magistrate of Jiaoshui in Laizhou and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wan was magistrate of Jiaoshui in Laizhou, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 齊少孤，依外家劉氏。

translations.literal: Qi was orphaned in youth and relied on the Liu family of his maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was orphaned young and lived with his maternal kin, the Liu family.

sentences.zh: 舉進士第一。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination ranking first.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi examination and ranked first.

sentences.zh: 儀狀俊偉，舉止端重，真宗見之，顧宰相寇準曰：“得人矣。”

translations.literal: His bearing was handsome and grand and his deportment dignified; Emperor Zhenzong saw him and turned to Grand Councilor Kou Zhun: "We have obtained a man."
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing and dignified in manner, he was presented to Zhenzong, who turned to Kou Zhun and said: "We have found our man."

sentences.zh: 詔金吾給七騶，傳呼以寵之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Golden Crow guard to give seven outrunners and ceremonial shouting to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Golden Crow guard to provide seven outrunners and ceremonial shouting in his honor.

sentences.zh: 狀元給騶，自齊始也。

translations.literal: Giving outrunners to the top graduate began with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The honor of outrunners for the top graduate began with Qi.

sentences.zh: 除將作監丞、通判袞州，徙濰州。

translations.literal: Appointed vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and supervisory commissioner of Yanzhou, then moved to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and supervisory commissioner of Yanzhou, then moved to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 以秘書省著作郎直集賢院。

translations.literal: As works officer of the Secretariat he was direct appointee of the Jixian collection.
translations.idiomatic: As works officer of the Secretariat he was direct appointee of the Jixian collection.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初，為司諫、修起居注，改尚書禮部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: Early in Renzong's reign, he served as remonstrance official and recorder of daily conduct, then was changed to vice director of ceremonial affairs in the Ministry of Rites with concurrent duty as associate censor handling miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Renzong's reign, he served as remonstrance official and recorder of daily conduct, then was made vice director of ceremonial affairs in the Ministry of Rites with concurrent duty as associate censor handling miscellaneous matters.

sentences.zh: 錢惟演守河陽，請曲賜鎮兵錢，章獻太后將許之。

translations.literal: When Qian Weiyan governed Heyang, he requested a special grant of funds for garrison troops; Empress Dowager Zhangxian was about to approve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Weiyan governed Heyang, he requested a special grant of funds for garrison troops, and Empress Dowager Zhangxian was about to approve it.

sentences.zh: 齊曰：“上新即位，惟演外戚，請偏賞以示私恩，不可許。”

translations.literal: Qi said: "The emperor has just ascended the throne. Weiyan is a maternal relative; he seeks a partial reward to display private favor—it must not be granted."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "The emperor has just ascended the throne. Weiyan is a maternal relative; he seeks a partial reward to show private favor—it must not be granted."

sentences.zh: 遂劾奏惟演。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized impeaching Weiyan.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized impeaching Weiyan.

sentences.zh: 以起居舍人知制誥，入為翰林學士，加侍讀學士。

translations.literal: As recorder of daily conduct he was made draft edict officer, entered service as academician of the Hanlin, and was given the additional title of reader academician.
translations.idiomatic: As recorder of daily conduct he was made draft edict officer, entered the Hanlin Academy as academician, and was given the additional title of reader academician.

sentences.zh: 太后大出金帛修景德寺，遣內侍羅崇勳主之，命齊為文記之。
