translations.literal: The empress dowager spent great sums of gold and silk to repair Jingde Temple, sent the inner attendant Luo Chongxun to oversee it, and ordered Qi to compose an inscription for it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager spent large sums of gold and silk to repair Jingde Temple, sent the inner attendant Luo Chongxun to oversee the work, and ordered Qi to compose an inscription for it.

sentences.zh: 崇勳陰使人誘齊曰：“趣為記，當得參知政事矣。”

translations.literal: Chongxun secretly sent someone to entice Qi, saying: "Hurry and compose the inscription—you will be made assistant administrator of affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun secretly sent someone to entice Qi, saying: "Hurry and write the inscription—you will be made assistant administrator of affairs."

sentences.zh: 齊久之不上，崇勳讒之，罷為龍圖閣學士、知河南府。

translations.literal: Qi for a long time did not submit it. Chongxun slandered him, and he was dismissed to academician of the Longtu collection and governor of Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qi long delayed submitting it. Chongxun slandered him, and he was dismissed to academician of the Longtu collection and governor of Henan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 參知政事魯宗道固爭留之，不能得。

translations.literal: Associate administrator Lu Zongdao firmly argued to retain him but could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Associate administrator Lu Zongdao firmly argued to keep him but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 以親老，改密州，徙應天府，召為右諫議大夫、御史中丞。

translations.literal: Because his parents were elderly, he was changed to Mizhou, moved to Yingtian prefecture, and summoned as right remonstrance grandee and censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Because his parents were elderly, he was transferred to Mizhou, then moved to Yingtian prefecture, and summoned as right remonstrance grandee and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，遺詔以楊太妃為皇太后，同裁制軍國事。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, the testamentary edict made Consort Yang empress dowager with joint authority over state and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager died, her testament made Consort Yang empress dowager with joint authority over state and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 閣門趣百官賀，齊使台吏毋追班，乃入白執政曰：“上春秋富，習知天下情偽，今始親政事，豈宜使女后相踵稱制乎！”

translations.literal: The Gate Office urged all officials to congratulate; Qi had the review office clerks not pursue the assembly, then entered to inform the chief ministers: "The emperor is in the prime of life and knows the truth and falsehood of the realm; he has just begun to handle government in person—how can another empress succeed in holding regency!"
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Office urged officials to congratulate. Qi told review clerks not to assemble the court, then told the chief ministers: "The emperor is young and vigorous and knows the realm's truths. He has just begun to rule in person—how can another empress succeed in regency?"

sentences.zh: 遂罷預政。

translations.literal: Thereupon joint government was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Joint government was at once abolished.

sentences.zh: 復為龍圖閣學士、權三司使。

translations.literal: Restored as academician of the Longtu Pavilion and acting commissioner of the Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as academician of the Longtu Pavilion and acting commissioner of the Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 有飛語傳荊王元儼為天下兵馬都元帥者，捕得繫獄，連逮甚眾。

translations.literal: There was a rumor that Prince Jing Wang Yuanyan was commander-in-chief of all armies under Heaven; the culprit was seized and imprisoned, and many were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: A rumor spread that Prince Jing Wang Yuanyan was commander-in-chief of all armies. The source was arrested and many were implicated.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，使齊按問之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent Qi to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and sent Qi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 齊曰：“此小人無知，不足治，且無以安荊王。”

translations.literal: Qi said: "This is a petty man's ignorance, not worth punishment, and moreover it cannot reassure Prince Jing."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "This is ignorant gossip, not worth prosecuting, and it will not reassure Prince Jing."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，遽釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and promptly released them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and released them at once.

sentences.zh: 拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice commissioner of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 交阯虐其部人，款宜州自歸者八百餘人，議者謂不可內。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi mistreated its tribesmen and more than eight hundred came to Yizhou offering submission; discussants said they could not be admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi abused its subjects and more than eight hundred came to Yizhou seeking refuge; officials said they should not be admitted.

sentences.zh: 齊曰：“蠻人去暴而歸有德，卻之不祥，請給荊湖閑田使自營；

translations.literal: Qi said: "The tribesmen leave violence and return to virtue; to reject them is inauspicious. I request idle fields in Jing and Hu be given for them to settle themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "They flee violence for virtue; to reject them is ill-omened. Give them idle fields in Jing and Hu to settle;

sentences.zh: 若縱去，當不復還舊部，必聚而為盜賊矣。”

translations.literal: if they are released to go, they will not return to their old tribes and will surely gather and become bandits."
translations.idiomatic: if we let them go they will not return home but gather as bandits."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: It was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not listen.

sentences.zh: 後數年，蠻果為亂。

translations.literal: Several years later the tribes indeed rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the tribes did rebel.

sentences.zh: 蜀大姓王齊雄坐殺人除名。

translations.literal: The great Shu clan Wang Qixiong was dismissed from office for murder.
translations.idiomatic: The great Shu clan Wang Qixiong was struck from office for murder.

sentences.zh: 齊雄，太后姻家，未更赦，復官。

translations.literal: Qixiong was kin to the empress dowager; before an amnesty had changed, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Qixiong was related to the empress dowager; before an amnesty could intervene his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 齊曰：“果如此，法撓矣！”

translations.literal: Qi said: "If it is truly thus, the law is bent!"
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "If this stands, the law is bent!"

sentences.zh: 明日，入奏事曰：“齊雄恃勢殺人，不死，又亟授以官，是以恩廢法也。”

translations.literal: The next day, entering to report affairs he said: "Qixiong relied on power to kill and was not executed, yet office was quickly granted again—this is using favor to abolish law."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he memorialized: "Qixiong killed by power and was not executed, yet office was quickly granted—favor has abolished law."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“降一等與官可乎？”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Would demoting one grade and granting office be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Would one grade lower suffice?"

sentences.zh: 齊曰：“以恩廢法，如朝廷何！”

translations.literal: Qi said: "Using favor to abolish law—what of the court!"
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "Using favor to abolish law—what becomes of the court!"

sentences.zh: 帝勉從之，乃抵齊雄罪。

translations.literal: The emperor reluctantly followed and thereupon charged Qixiong's crime.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reluctantly agreed and charged Qixiong.

sentences.zh: 錢惟演附丁謂，樞密題名，輒削去寇準姓氏，云“逆準不書”。

translations.literal: Qian Weiyan attached himself to Ding Wei; on the military affairs roster he always cut out Kou Zhun's surname, saying "the rebel Zhun is not written."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weiyan attached to Ding Wei; on the military affairs roster he cut out Kou Zhun's name, writing "rebel Zhun not recorded."

sentences.zh: 齊言於仁宗曰：“寇準忠義聞天下，社稷之臣也，豈可為奸黨所誣哉！”

translations.literal: Qi spoke to Emperor Renzong: "Kou Zhun's loyalty and righteousness are known throughout the realm; he was a minister of the altars of state—how can he be slandered by a wicked faction!"
translations.idiomatic: Qi told Renzong: "Kou Zhun's loyalty is known throughout the realm. He was a pillar of state—how can a wicked faction slander him!"

sentences.zh: 仁宗遽令磨去。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong immediately ordered it scraped away.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong immediately ordered the slander erased.

sentences.zh: 郭皇后廢，將立富人陳氏女為后，齊極論之。

translations.literal: When Empress Guo was deposed and the rich man's daughter of the Chen clan was to be established as empress, Qi argued forcefully against it.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Guo was deposed and a rich man's daughter of the Chen clan was to be made empress, Qi argued forcefully against it.

sentences.zh: 拜禮部侍郎、參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of rites and Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of rites and vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 契丹祭天於幽州，以兵屯境上。

translations.literal: The Khitan sacrificed to Heaven at Youzhou and stationed troops on the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sacrificed at Youzhou and massed troops on the border.

sentences.zh: 輔臣欲調兵備邊，與齊迭議帝前，齊畫三策，料契丹必不叛盟。

translations.literal: The chief ministers wished to transfer troops to guard the border and debated with Qi before the emperor in turn; Qi drew three strategies and judged the Khitan would surely not break the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers wished to mobilize border troops and debated with Qi before the emperor; Qi laid out three strategies and judged the Khitan would not break the alliance.

sentences.zh: 王曾與齊善，曾與夷簡不相能，曾罷相，齊亦以戶部侍郎歸班。

translations.literal: Wang Zeng was friendly with Qi; Zeng and Lü Yijian could not get along; when Zeng was dismissed from the chancellorship, Qi also returned to the ranks as vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zeng was friendly with Qi; Zeng and Lü Yijian clashed; when Zeng left the chancellorship, Qi also returned as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋出知潁州，卒，年五十二，贈兵部尚書，諡曰文忠。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as prefect of Yingzhou and died at age fifty-two; posthumously made minister of war with the posthumous title Wenzhong (Cultured and Loyal).
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went out as prefect of Yingzhou and died at fifty-two. He was posthumously made minister of war with the posthumous title Wenzhong (Cultured and Loyal).

sentences.zh: 潁人見其故吏朱采會喪，猶號泣思之。

translations.literal: The people of Ying, seeing his former clerk Zhu Cai at the mourning assembly, still wept and thought of him.
translations.idiomatic: People of Ying, seeing his former clerk Zhu Cai at the funeral, still wept for him.

sentences.zh: 齊方重有風采，性謙退，不妄言。

translations.literal: Qi was square, weighty, and had presence; his nature was modest and retiring and he did not speak rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was square, dignified, and commanding, yet modest and sparing of words.

sentences.zh: 有善未嘗自伐。

translations.literal: When he had done good he never boasted of himself.
translations.idiomatic: He never boasted of his own good deeds.

sentences.zh: 丁謂秉政，欲齊附己，齊終不往。

translations.literal: When Ding Wei held power he wished Qi to attach to him; Qi in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Wei held power he wanted Qi's support; Qi never went to him.

sentences.zh: 少與徐人劉顏善，顏罪廢，齊上其書數十萬言，得復官。

translations.literal: In youth he was friendly with Liu Yan of Xuzhou; Yan's crime led to dismissal; Qi submitted his writings of several hundred thousand characters and Yan was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he befriended Liu Yan of Xuzhou. When Yan was dismissed for a crime, Qi submitted his writings—hundreds of thousands of characters—and Yan was restored.

sentences.zh: 顏卒，又以女妻其子庠。

translations.literal: When Yan died he also gave his daughter in marriage to Yan's son Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan died he gave his daughter to Yan's son Xiang in marriage.

sentences.zh: 所薦龐籍、楊偕、劉隨、段少連，後率為名臣。

translations.literal: Those he recommended—Pang Ji, Yang Xie, Liu Sui, and Duan Shaolian—later all became famous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Men he recommended—Pang Ji, Yang Xie, Liu Sui, and Duan Shaolian—later all became famous ministers.

sentences.zh: 始，齊無子，以從子延慶為後。

translations.literal: At first Qi had no son and took his younger clansman Yanqing as heir.
translations.idiomatic: At first Qi had no son and adopted his clansman Yanqing.

sentences.zh: 既歿，有遺腹子曰延嗣。

translations.literal: After he died there was a posthumous son named Yansi.
translations.idiomatic: After his death a posthumous son named Yansi was born.

sentences.zh: 〈從子〉

translations.literal: 〈Younger clansman〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Younger clansman〉

sentences.zh: 延慶

translations.literal: Yanqing
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing

sentences.zh: 延慶字仲遠，中進士第，通判明州。

translations.literal: Yanqing, styled Zhongyuan, passed the jinshi examination and was supervisory commissioner of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing, whose courtesy name was Zhongyuan, passed the jinshi examination and was supervisory commissioner of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 曆福建路轉運判官，提點京東、陝西刑獄。

translations.literal: He served as transport judge of Fujian circuit and judicial intendant of Jingdong and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as transport judge of Fujian circuit and judicial intendant of Jingdong and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 神宗初，以集賢校理曆開封府推官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shenzong's reign, as collator of the Jixian collection he served as Kaifeng judicial officer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenzong's reign, as Jixian collator he served as Kaifeng judicial officer.

sentences.zh: 有衛士告黃衣老卒筒火入直，延慶察卒色辭，疑焉，詢之，果為所誣，即反坐告者。

translations.literal: A guardsman reported an old soldier in yellow clothes carrying fire into duty; Yanqing observed the soldier's expression and words, doubted it, questioned him, and it was indeed a false accusation; he immediately reversed the charge on the accuser.
translations.idiomatic: A guardsman reported an old soldier in yellow carrying fire on duty. Yanqing studied his face and words, doubted the report, questioned him, found a false accusation, and punished the accuser.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝重之，加直史館、知河中府。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported the emperor valued him and added direct appointment to the History Office and prefect of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported the emperor valued him, made him direct historian, and prefect of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 明年，同修起居注，直舍人院、判流內銓，拜天章閣待制、秦鳳等路都轉運使，以應辦熙河軍須功，進龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: The next year he jointly compiled the imperial diary, was direct appointee of the Drafting Office and judge of the mobile selection office, appointed awaiting academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion and overall transport commissioner of Qinfeng and other circuits; for merit in supplying the Hexi army he was promoted to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he compiled the imperial diary, drafted edicts, judged the mobile selection office, became Tianzhang awaiting academician and overall transport commissioner of Qinfeng circuits, and was promoted to direct Longtu academician for supplying the Hexi army.

sentences.zh: 王韶進師河州，羌斷其歸路。

translations.literal: Wang Shao advanced troops to Hezhou and the Qiang cut his return route.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao advanced on Hezhou and the Qiang cut his retreat.

sentences.zh: 延慶曰：“兵事非吾所宜預，然主帥在難，不急援之，恐敗國事。”

translations.literal: Yanqing said: "Military affairs are not what I should intervene in, yet the commander is in peril; if we do not hurry to rescue, I fear state affairs will fail."
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing said: "Military affairs are not my province, but the commander is trapped. If we do not rescue him quickly, the campaign may fail."

sentences.zh: 遂檄兵赴救，羌解去，韶得全師還。

translations.literal: He thereupon dispatched troops to rescue; the Qiang dispersed and Shao returned with his whole army.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched troops; the Qiang withdrew and Shao returned intact.

sentences.zh: 轉運判官蔡蒙劾其擅興，朝廷問知狀，易蒙他道。

translations.literal: Transport judge Cai Meng impeached him for acting on his own authority; the court asked who knew the facts and changed Meng to another circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Transport judge Cai Meng impeached him for unauthorized action; the court questioned witnesses and transferred Meng elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 韶入朝，延慶攝熙帥。

translations.literal: When Shao entered court, Yanqing acted as acting Xi commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao came to court, Yanqing acted as commander of Xi.

sentences.zh: 元夕張燈，羌乘隙伏兵北關下，遣其種二十九人偽請來屬，將舉火內應。

translations.literal: On the Yuan festival night lamps were hung; the Qiang seized the chance to ambush troops below the north gate and sent twenty-nine of their tribesmen falsely requesting to submit, intending to light fires as internal response.
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Festival the Qiang ambushed below the north gate and sent twenty-nine tribesmen feigning submission, planning an internal rising by fire.

sentences.zh: 延慶覘知，悉斬以徇，伏者宵潰。

translations.literal: Yanqing detected it, executed them all as a warning, and the ambushers fled at night.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing detected the plot, executed all twenty-nine as a warning, and the ambushers fled by night.

sentences.zh: 蕃官詐稱木征欲降，邀大將景思立來迎。

translations.literal: A tribal officer falsely claimed Muzheng wished to surrender and invited the great general Jing Sil to come welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: A tribal officer falsely claimed Muzheng wished to surrender and invited general Jing Sil to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 延慶命毋輒出，即違節制，雖有功亦誅，思立不從，卒敗死。

translations.literal: Yanqing ordered that none go out rashly; even if one disobeyed regulations yet had merit he would still be executed. Sil did not obey and in the end was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing ordered no one to go out rashly: even merit would not save disobedience. Sil went anyway and was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 徙知成都府兼兵馬都鈐轄。

translations.literal: Transferred to prefect of Chengdu and concurrent overall military commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Chengdu and concurrent overall military commander.

sentences.zh: 本道舊不置都鈐轄，至是特命之。

translations.literal: This circuit had not previously had an overall commander; to this point he was specially appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit had never had such a commander; he was specially appointed.

sentences.zh: 茂州羈縻州蠻族九，自推一人為將統其眾，將常在州聽要束。

translations.literal: Maozhou had nine dependent tribal states; they themselves chose one man as general to command the masses; the general always remained in the prefecture subject to restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhou had nine dependent tribal states that chose their own leader; the leader always remained in the prefecture under restraint.

sentences.zh: 州居群蠻中，無城塹，惟樹鹿角為固。

translations.literal: The prefecture lay amid many tribes, had no walls or moats, and only planted palisades of antlers for defense.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lay amid tribes without walls or moats, defended only by antler palisades.

sentences.zh: 蠻屢夜入剽人畜，徼貨來贖。

translations.literal: The tribes often entered by night to plunder people and livestock and extorted goods for ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes often raided by night for people and livestock and extorted ransom.

sentences.zh: 民患苦，詣郡守李琪請築城。

translations.literal: The people suffered and went to prefect Li Qi requesting walls be built.
translations.idiomatic: The people suffered and asked prefect Li Qi to build walls.

sentences.zh: 琪上於朝，詔延慶度其利便，延慶下其事，琪已去。

translations.literal: Qi memorialized to court; an edict ordered Yanqing to assess the advantage; Yanqing referred the matter downward and Qi had already left.
translations.idiomatic: Qi memorialized; the court ordered Yanqing to assess the project. Yanqing referred it downward, but Qi had already left.

sentences.zh: 後守範百常以為利，築之。

translations.literal: Later prefect Fan Baichang thought it profitable and built them.
translations.idiomatic: Later prefect Fan Baichang thought it worthwhile and built the walls.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋訴謂侵其土地，乞罷築，不許。

translations.literal: The tribal chiefs complained that their land was invaded and begged to stop construction; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal chiefs complained of encroachment and begged to halt construction; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 蠻數百奄至，拒卻之。

translations.literal: Several hundred tribesmen suddenly arrived and were repelled.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred tribesmen attacked and were repelled.

sentences.zh: 明日，又大至，盡焚鹿角及民盧舍，引梯衝攻牙城，百常扞禦，殺二蠻酋，乃退。

translations.literal: The next day they came again in force, burned all the antler palisades and commoners' houses, brought ladders and rams to assault the yamen city; Baichang defended, killed two tribal chiefs, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they returned in force, burned palisades and houses, and assaulted the yamen with ladders and rams. Baichang defended, killed two chiefs, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 然遊騎猶繞四山，南北路皆為所據，城中不敢出。

translations.literal: Yet roaming horsemen still circled the four mountains; north and south roads were all held by them and the city dared not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming horsemen still held the surrounding hills; roads north and south were cut and the city dared not venture out.

sentences.zh: 百常募人間道告急於成都。

translations.literal: Baichang recruited men by secret paths to report urgently to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Baichang sent messengers by secret paths to Chengdu for help.

sentences.zh: 延慶命與之和，奏乞遣近上內臣共經蠻事。

translations.literal: Yanqing ordered peace made with them and memorialized requesting a nearby inner attendant be sent jointly to manage tribal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing ordered peace talks and asked the court to send a senior inner attendant to manage tribal affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔押班王中正往，中正受旨，凡軍事皆令與都鈐轄議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Escort Officer Wang Zhongzheng to go; Zhongzheng received instructions that all military affairs were to be discussed with the overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent escort officer Wang Zhongzheng with orders that all military affairs be discussed with the overall commander.

sentences.zh: 將行，言茂去成都遠，一一與議，慮失事機，請得專決。

translations.literal: About to depart, he said Maozhou was far from Chengdu; to discuss everything one by one feared losing the moment; he requested sole decision.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he said Maozhou was far from Chengdu; joint consultation would lose time, and he asked sole authority.

sentences.zh: 於是事無巨細皆自處，延慶不復預。

translations.literal: Thereupon affairs great and small were all decided by himself; Yanqing no longer participated.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he decided everything himself and Yanqing had no further role.

sentences.zh: 監司附中正，奏延慶區理失宜，致生邊患。

translations.literal: Supervisory officials attached to Zhongzheng and memorialized that Yanqing's regional management was improper and had produced border troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory officials sided with Zhongzheng and memorialized that Yanqing's management had caused border trouble.

sentences.zh: 徙知渭州，仍降為天章閣待制。

translations.literal: Transferred to prefect of Weizhou, he was still demoted to Tianzhang awaiting academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Weizhou and demoted to Tianzhang awaiting academician.

sentences.zh: 夏人禹臧苑麻疑邊境有謀，使人入塞賣馬，吏執以告。

translations.literal: The Xia man Yu Zang Yuanma suspected border plots and sent a man into the frontier to sell horses; officials seized and reported him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia leader Yu Zang Yuanma suspected border plots and sent a man to sell horses inside the frontier; officials seized him.

sentences.zh: 延慶曰：“彼疑，故來覘。

translations.literal: Yanqing said: "He suspects, hence he comes to spy.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing said: "He suspects us, so he comes to spy.

sentences.zh: 執之，是成其疑。”

translations.literal: To seize him is to confirm his suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: Seizing him only confirms his suspicion."

sentences.zh: 約馬直授之使去。

translations.literal: He agreed on horse price and handed it to the envoy to let him go.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed a fair price and let the envoy go.

sentences.zh: 疆吏入敵境攘羊馬，得而戮諸境上，且告之曰：“兩境不相侵，則相保以安，故戮以戒。

translations.literal: Border officials entering enemy territory to seize sheep and horses, when they obtained them executed them on the border and also informed them: "When the two borders do not invade each other they protect each other in peace; hence execution as warning.
translations.idiomatic: When border officials seized sheep and horses in enemy territory, he had them executed on the border with notice: "Peace requires mutual non-aggression; this execution is a warning.

sentences.zh: 若有之，亦當爾也。”

translations.literal: If there is such conduct on your side, it will be treated likewise."
translations.idiomatic: If you do the same, we will do the same."

sentences.zh: 夏人悅服。

translations.literal: The Xia people were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia were satisfied.

sentences.zh: 嘗得《安南行軍法》讀之，仿其製，部分正兵弓箭手人馬，團為九將，合百隊，分左右前後四部。

translations.literal: He once obtained Annan Campaign Methods and read it; imitating its system he arranged regular troops, archers, and horse teams into nine generals combining a hundred companies, divided into left, right, front, and rear four sections.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Annan Campaign Methods, he modeled his forces: regular troops and archers in nine generals commanding a hundred companies in four sections.

sentences.zh: 隊有駐戰、拓戰之別，步騎器械，每將皆同。

translations.literal: Companies had the distinction of holding battle and expanding battle; infantry, cavalry, and weapons were the same for each general.
translations.idiomatic: Companies were designated for holding or expanding battle; each general's infantry, cavalry, and arms matched.

sentences.zh: 以蕃兵人馬為別隊，各隨所近分隸焉。

translations.literal: Tribal soldiers and horses were a separate company, each attached according to proximity.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal troops formed separate companies attached by proximity.

sentences.zh: 諸將之數，不及正兵之半，乃所以制之。

translations.literal: The number of generals did not reach half the regular troops—this was how to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal generals numbered less than half the regular force—by design, to control them.

sentences.zh: 處老弱於城砦，較其遠近而為區別。

translations.literal: The old and weak were placed in fortresses, comparing distance to make distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: The old and weak were placed in fortresses according to distance.

sentences.zh: 使蕃、漢無得相雜，以防其變。

translations.literal: Tribal and Han were not allowed to mix, to guard against mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal and Han troops were kept separate to prevent mutiny.

sentences.zh: 具為書上之。

translations.literal: He fully set it out in a book and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote it up fully and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 時鄜延呂惠卿亦分畫兵，延慶條其不便，神宗善其議。

translations.literal: At the time Lü Huiqing of Fuyan also divided troops; Yanqing listed its inconveniences and Emperor Shenzong approved his argument.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Huiqing of Fuyan also reorganized troops, Yanqing listed the flaws and Shenzong approved his view.

sentences.zh: 召知開封府，拜翰林學士。

translations.literal: Summoned as prefect of Kaifeng, he was appointed Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as prefect of Kaifeng, he was made Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 以言者罷知滁州，曆瀛、洪州，復龍圖閣待制，帥高陽。

translations.literal: Because of critics he was dismissed to prefect of Chuzhou, served Ying and Hong prefectures, restored as Longtu awaiting academician, and commanded Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Critics removed him to Chuzhou; he served Ying and Hong, was restored as Longtu awaiting academician, and commanded Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 閱歲，復直學士，移定武。

translations.literal: After a year he was again direct academician and moved to Dingwu.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was again direct academician and moved to Dingwu.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，入為工部、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era he entered as vice minister of works and vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanyou era he entered as vice minister of works and personnel.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二，賜錢三十萬，官庀其葬。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-two; thirty thousand cash was bestowed and officials arranged his burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two; the court granted thirty thousand cash and arranged his burial.

sentences.zh: 延慶有學問，平居簡嘿，遇事能別白是非，所至有惠政。

translations.literal: Yanqing had learning; in ordinary life he was terse and silent; on affairs he could distinguish right and wrong; wherever he went he had benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing was learned, quiet in daily life, clear in judgment, and benevolent in every post.

sentences.zh: 既為伯父齊後，齊晚得子，乃歸其宗，籍家所有付之，無一毫自予，萊人義焉。

translations.literal: Having become heir to his uncle Qi, when Qi late in life had a son he returned to his clan; he registered all the household property and gave it to him, not keeping a single item for himself—the people of Lai praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted as Qi's heir, when Qi late in life had a son of his own Yanqing returned to his birth clan and gave Qi all family property without keeping a penny—men of Lai praised his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 論曰：章獻太后稱制時，群臣多希合用事，魯宗道、薛奎、蔡齊參預其間，正色孤立，無所回撓。

translations.literal: The discussion says: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian held power, many ministers curried favor to follow those in power; Lu Zongdao, Xue Kui, and Cai Qi participated in government, stern in color and isolated, bending to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The historians say: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian held power, many ministers curried favor. Lu Zongdao, Xue Kui, and Cai Qi stood apart, unbending.

sentences.zh: 宗道能沮劉氏七廟之議，奎正母后袞冕為非禮，齊從容一言絕女后相踵稱制之患，真所謂以道事君者歟！

translations.literal: Zongdao could thwart the Liu seven-temples proposal; Kui corrected the empress dowager's dragon robe and coronet as improper rites; Qi with a calm word ended the harm of empresses succeeding in regency—they are truly those who served their ruler by the Way!
translations.idiomatic: Zongdao blocked the Liu ancestral temples; Kui condemned the empress dowager's imperial robes; Qi with one calm sentence ended successive female regency—they truly served their ruler by the Way.

sentences.zh: 曙辨奸斷獄，為時良吏，在位又多薦拔名臣，若請群臣立家廟以復古禮，皆知為政之本焉。

translations.literal: Shu discerned treachery and judged prisons and was a good official of the time; in office he also recommended many famous ministers; in requesting that the hundred officials establish family temples to restore ancient rites—all knew the root of governing.
translations.idiomatic: Shu discerned fraud and judged cases as a model official of his age, recommended many famous ministers in office, and in asking officials to restore family temples showed he knew the root of governance.
